title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & hygiene
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Our combined CI workflows are large and slow to iterate on. Tests, linting, and release automation are coupled which increases CI runtime and makes cache behavior brittle. This PR splits the monolithic workflow into three focused workflows (lint, test, release), extracts cache key logic into a shared action, and applies a set of repo-hygiene changes (action bumps, node runtime pinning, and doc updates).

What changed (high level):
- Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into .github/workflows/lint.yml, test.yml, and release.yml to reduce runtime and improve isolation for flakiness debugging.
- Introduced .github/workflows/common/cache-keys.yml and a small composite action scripts/ci/cache-key.sh to centralize cache key generation (commit+lockfile+deps fingerprint).
- Bumped primary GH Actions and Node tool versions: actions/checkout@v3 -> v4, actions/setup-node pinned to 20.x in test/release workflows and 18.x in legacy-docs workflow.
- Reworked job matrices to avoid unnecessary permutations (split lint matrix from test matrix).
- Added dedicated step-level caching for Python venvs (docs build) and node_modules across workspace packages; tuned cache restore/save placement to reduce cache misses.
- Reduced concurrency group window and added cancel-in-progress to keep PR runs fresh.
- Minor repo hygiene: updated docs/ci.md, removed deprecated scripts/ci/old-cache.sh, and corrected a few linter rule overrides.

Checklist: 
- [x] Split workflows and validate triggers
- [x] Centralize cache key logic and add unit tests for key generator script
- [x] Bump GH actions and verify matrix runs
- [x] Update docs and team runbook

Risks/Notes:
- Release workflow changes are guarded behind a dry-run flag and protected by required approvals.
- Cache key changes may cause initial misses; expected one warm run to populate.
- Node version pinning kept intentionally conservative for docs build (18.x) to avoid spurious breakage.

References: Linear ENG-10234 (CI stability), ENG-10567 (release automation hygiene).
